meta.description: An open research project that forecasts where Bitcoin is heading in 1, 4 and 24 hours and checks every forecast against what actually happened. Not investment advice.

footer.disclaimer: A study and research project. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy, sell or hold anything. Forecasts are experiments and are often wrong.

fc.title: Forecasts, checked in public
fc.intro: Every hour the model says whether Bitcoin will be higher or lower in 1, 4 and 24 hours, and how much the price should swing. When the time comes, the forecast is compared with what happened and lands in the table below, next to simple rules that need no model at all.
fc.caveat: In tests on 2019–2026 data, the direction forecasts were no better than those simple rules, while the swing forecasts were clearly better. Both stay public so anyone can follow how they do from now on.
fc.score_note: Share of forecasts that got the direction right, for the model and for two rules that need no model: always saying up, and always saying the opposite of the last move. Swing error is the average gap between the forecast swing and the real one, in percentage points (lower is better). The best in each group is highlighted.
fc.log_note: Last 7 days, newest first. The swing column shows the forecast swing next to the real one.
fc.bt_note: Month by month, the model is trained only on the 3 years before each month and tested on that month.
fc.cmp_aria: Chart comparing each forecast with what happened. Point or tap a column for details.

about.title: About the model
about.p1: Where Is My Crypto Going? is an open study and research project by Victor Miranda Florido (Universidade Federal Fluminense). It asks a simple question: can public data say where Bitcoin is heading in the next hours? Everything is free to inspect: the data, the code and every forecast ever made.
about.p2: The answer so far is mostly no for the direction of the price, and the site shows that openly. The size of the swings, on the other hand, is predictable to a useful degree.
about.data_price: Price: BTC-USD candles from Coinbase, minute by minute since July 2015, grouped into hours.
about.data_fg: Sentiment: the Crypto Fear & Greed Index from alternative.me, daily since February 2018.
about.data_news: News: counts and tone of news about Bitcoin and about world topics (interest rates, markets, regulation, cyber attacks, wars, sanctions), hour by hour since 2015, from the GDELT Project.
about.data_gap: Known gap: before 16 November 2026, the hourly news counts come from GDELT's copy in Google BigQuery, which misses whole files in about a quarter of the hours. From that date on, the files are read directly and are complete.
about.model_p1: Two models, both gradient-boosted decision trees, for 1, 4 and 24 hours ahead:
about.model_dir: Direction: the chance that the price will be higher, from price features only (recent returns, swings, range and volume). News and sentiment were tested and added nothing.
about.model_vol: Swing (volatility): how much the price should move, from price features, the market state and past volatility over the last hour, day, week and month.
about.model_train: Retraining: on the first day of each month, on the most recent 3 years. A new model only replaces the current one if its month-by-month test is not worse.
about.f_ret: Return over h hours: r = ln(P(t+h) / P(t)), from the close of the last finished hour.
about.f_vol: Swing over h hours: σ = √(Σ rᵢ²), the square root of the sum of squared hourly returns, in %.
about.f_regime: Regime: bull if the 50-day average price is above the 200-day average, bear otherwise. A common convention that confirms turns only weeks later.
about.f_state: Swings label: the last 24 hours of volatility ranked against the past year (calm below 25%, volatile above 75%, extreme above 95%).
about.check_p1: Forecasts are written once and never edited. When their time comes they are compared with the real price, next to rules that need no model:
about.ref_up: Always up: Bitcoin rose in a little over half of all hours, so saying up every time already beats a coin flip.
about.ref_rev: Opposite of the last move: if the last hour went up, say down. This rule alone was right 53% of the time at 1 hour.
about.ref_vol: For swings: repeat the swing of the last hours, and the HAR model, the standard reference in finance research.
about.found_dir: Direction: about 54% right at 1 hour, but the opposite-of-the-last-move rule gets 53%, and the edge has been shrinking year after year. At 24 hours, no model beat simply saying up.
about.found_vol: Swings: the model's error is 20–25% smaller than repeating recent swings and 4–8% smaller than the HAR model.
about.found_extra: Neural networks (a dense network and a recurrent one that reads the last 168 hours) did no better than the decision trees.
about.lim1: Markets change. A pattern that held in the past can vanish, and these models can be wrong for long stretches.
about.lim2: Forecasts use the close of each hour; real trades happen at other prices and carry costs far larger than the edges measured here.
about.lim3: This is research, not advice. Nothing here suggests buying, selling or holding Bitcoin or anything else.

js.regime_text_bull: The 50-day average price ({ma50}) is above the 200-day average ({ma200}), so by this common rule the market is in a bull phase. The rule is slow: right now the price is {dd} below its 1-year high.
js.regime_text_bear: The 50-day average price ({ma50}) is below the 200-day average ({ma200}), so by this common rule the market is in a bear phase. The price is {dd} below its 1-year high.
js.nothing_checked: No forecast has been checked yet
js.too_few: Still far too few forecasts to judge; differences of a few points mean nothing yet.
js.bt_period: Tested month by month from {from} to {to}, model {model}. Each month uses a model trained only on the 3 years before it.
js.cmp_note_ret: Each column is one forecast from the last 7 days. The bar is how much the price really moved; the cross is the move the model expected. The model's expected moves sit close to zero: it rarely calls big moves.
js.cmp_note_vol: Each column is one forecast from the last 7 days. The bar is how much the price really swung; the cross is the model's forecast and the square is the simple rule of repeating the last swing. The closer the marker is to the top of the bar, the smaller the miss.
js.cmp_note_acc: Share of right directions since launch, forecast after forecast, for the model and for the two rules that need no model. With few forecasts the lines jump around a lot.
